findings.source_claim: Lecture22 is about magnetic matter; indexed L28 has a broader combined title.
findings.assessment: The actual 27-page PDF is the source identity. Page6 only recalls radiation energy/momentum, Poynting vector, transmission lines and scattering from the previous lecture; it does not supply new derivations for those topics.
findings.basis: Direct full-source reading.

findings.source_claim: Exam schedule, grading, preparation and scoring statements.
findings.assessment: These are contemporaneous course statements, not independently established historical outcomes or current policy. Three perfect equally weighted problems out of four give 75% of the exam. The separate 35 course points and listed quiz/makeup points are different quantities; the source does not give a complete course-grade allocation. Sleep advice and motivational claims are not physics findings. No historical outcome inferred.
findings.basis: Direct reading and 3/4 arithmetic.

findings.source_claim: Electrons rotate on orbits; molecular quantum structure totally determines magnetism.
findings.assessment: A prescribed orbit is a classical current-loop model, not a literal account of atomic trajectories. Equilibrium material magnetism requires quantum orbital/spin/band structure and interactions. Macroscopic response also depends on temperature, geometry, defects and history, not molecular identity alone. Spin is intrinsic angular momentum, not literal spinning charge. Random orbit orientation is not a universal explanation of cancellation; filled-shell quantum cancellation differs from random orientations of existing moments.
findings.basis: Model distinction, source scope and official quantum-magnetism account.

findings.source_claim: I=ev/(2πr), μ=IA/c=evr/(2c); L=r×p; μ=-eL/(2m_e c).
findings.assessment: Correct for a nonrelativistic prescribed circular electron orbit with e>0, p=m_e v and Gaussian units; I and μ without arrows are magnitudes. Conventional current opposes electron velocity. Page8 shows v left and I right at the back of the ellipse, giving downward loop field with the ordinary perspective/right-hand convention; μ is antiparallel to electron L. The factor 1/c is absent in the SI loop moment. The formula is orbital; the spin coefficient differs by g_s≈2.0023 in μ_s=-g_s e S/(2m_e c), where g_s is defined positive.
findings.basis: Independent period/current/area/angular-momentum calculation and right-hand rule; NIST electron g-factor sign convention noted.

findings.source_claim: Lenz law rearranges orbits to oppose external B; all orbital contributions reduce field.
findings.assessment: The induced diamagnetic contribution opposes an applied-field increase; the page8 B_ext right/B_induced left arrows express that sign. Lenz law is fundamentally about flux change, not a general equilibrium derivation of material susceptibility or exclusion of all static field. Permanent orbital moments may also contribute to paramagnetism; the spin-versus-orbit dichotomy is incomplete. Spell Lenz, not Lentz.
findings.basis: Induction-sign audit and quantum-model distinction.

findings.source_claim: τ=μ×B tends to line moments up and strengthen B.
findings.assessment: The torque formula is correct in Gaussian and SI units. For an isolated fixed-magnitude moment with μ=γL, it gives precession at fixed angle to constant B, not relaxation into alignment. Energy U=-μ·B favors parallel μ, but thermal equilibration/dissipation is needed for net equilibrium alignment. Page10 parallel rightward arrows correctly depict a positive magnetization contribution under the stated response model.
findings.basis: Independent dμ/dt=γ μ×B, hence d(μ·B)/dt=0 for fixed B; equilibrium-energy deduction.

findings.source_claim: Three categories; χ<0 diamagnetic, χ>0 paramagnetic.
findings.assessment: Signs classify weak linear dia/paramagnetic response, but positive χ alone does not define a paramagnetic phase. Ferromagnets and other ordered systems may have positive differential response. Antiferromagnetism and ferrimagnetism are omitted; this is a selected introductory classification, not exhaustive.
findings.basis: Constitutive-law scope and official ordered-phase material.

findings.source_claim: Inside field always weaker for diamagnets and stronger for paramagnets; H is external field.
findings.assessment: M opposes or augments local H in an isotropic linear material. Comparing B inside with a field outside requires geometry and boundary conditions. In SI an ellipsoid has H_int=H_applied-N M and B_int/B0=(1+χ)/(1+Nχ); for an infinite slab normal to field N=1 gives B_int=B0, despite nonzero M. H is not generally the bare field of free currents, since ∇·H=-4π∇·M in Gaussian units.
findings.basis: Independent boundary/ellipsoid deduction.

findings.source_claim: Diamagnets are expelled, paramagnets pulled into B; aluminum orients parallel.
findings.assessment: For a small weak isotropic body in vacuum F≈χ_SI V∇(B0²)/(2μ0): negative χ moves toward weaker field and positive χ toward stronger field. Uniform field produces no net translational force in that approximation. M parallel/antiparallel to field does not alone determine the long-axis orientation of a body: anisotropy, shape, suspension and field profile matter. Page14 has a rightward gap field but no pole labels or pivot details. If pole senses are inferred from the gap arrows, left face is N and right face S; this is a diagram deduction, not a statement about actual apparatus. Bismuth orientation cannot be uniquely deduced from this drawing.
findings.basis: Independent energy-gradient and μ×B argument; no undocumented demo outcome inferred.

findings.source_claim: Paired orbitals imply diamagnetism; Na, Al, NiSO4 examples; oxygen is an exception requiring liquid state.
findings.assessment: H2O, Cu, NaCl, Bi and ordinary normal-state Pb/diamond are consistent diamagnetic examples, while Na/Al and ordinary-temperature NiSO4 are paramagnetic examples. Atomic pairing alone is insufficient for metals; bands and conduction electrons matter. Page13 heading saying examples of diamagnetic materials is a typo for paramagnetic. O2 has two unpaired molecular-orbital electrons and is paramagnetic as a gas as well as a liquid; thermal motion reduces response but does not wipe it out. Page18 itself lists positive gas-O2 susceptibility. Liquid density/cooling makes the effect easier to demonstrate. Composition, phase and temperature qualify all examples; Pb below its superconducting transition is a different regime.
findings.basis: Source internal contradiction, molecular-orbital account and direct gas measurement.

findings.source_claim: M is magnetic moment per unit volume; μ=MV; [M]=[B]; B=H+4πM; vacuum B=H.
findings.assessment: Definitions and Gaussian dimension relation are correct. μ=MV requires uniform M; generally μ=∫M dV. M has magnetic-moment/volume units (emu/cm³ in Gaussian magnetic usage), while H is in oersted and B in gauss. In SI M,H are A/m, B is tesla and B=μ0(H+M), so [M]=[B] and B=H are not SI statements. 4πM, not M alone, is the Gaussian additive term; even this decomposition is not a geometry-independent field-of-material separation.
findings.basis: Independent dimensional and integral check.

findings.source_claim: ∇×H=4πJ_free/c; ∇×M=J_bound/c; ∇×B=4π(J_free+J_bound)/c.
findings.assessment: Algebra and factors are correct for magnetostatics with magnetization bound volume current J_M=c∇×M. Include surface current K_M=c M×n at a discontinuity; uniform bulk M does not imply no field. In time-dependent macroscopic electrodynamics ∇×H=4πJ_free/c+(1/c)∂D/∂t and bound current also includes ∂P/∂t. Free means the chosen free/bound decomposition, not every current an experimenter can control.
findings.basis: Independent curl substitution and displacement/polarization-current accounting.

findings.source_claim: Printed H=χ_m M followed by B=H(1+4πχ_m).
findings.assessment: First equation is reversed: M=χ_m H is the susceptibility definition. Keeping the printed first equation would yield B=H(1+4π/χ_m) for nonzero χ_m. The displayed final B formula is correct only with the corrected definition, linear isotropic scalar response, Gaussian susceptibility and internal H. Anisotropic response uses a tensor; hysteretic ferro-response is not a single constant χ.
findings.basis: Independent substitution and χ→0 vacuum limit.

findings.source_claim: Table χ_m in 10^-5: U40, Al2.2, O2gas0.2, H2O-0.9, Pb-1.8, diamond-2.1, Bi-16.6.
findings.assessment: The numerical scale is consistent with SI volume susceptibilities, especially water and gas oxygen, whereas surrounding formulas use Gaussian χ. Thus SI convention is a strong evidence-based inference, not printed metadata. χ_SI=4πχ_G; inserting these entries directly into the Gaussian formula overstates μr-1 by 4π. All seven signs, exponents and conversions are audited in independent-calculations.json. No source, temperature, gas pressure, purity, crystalline direction or uncertainties are supplied; exact values for all seven are not independently certified. NIST water at 22°C is about -9.0559e-6 SI; measured gaseous O2 molar susceptibility yields 1.784e-6 SI at assumed ideal-gas 293.15K/1atm, supporting the rounded 2e-6 scale.
findings.basis: Direct transcription; independent full-table conversion; two quantitative primary/official checks.

findings.source_claim: Ferromagnetism is extra-strong paramagnetism; nonlinearity distinguishes it.
findings.assessment: This is an analogy, not a definition. Interactions permit spontaneous ordered magnetization below Tc; domains can make a macroscopic sample nearly unmagnetized. Even noninteracting spin moments have nonlinear M=nμ tanh(μB/kBT) and saturate, so nonlinearity alone does not distinguish phases. Remanence/hysteresis are history-dependent and not guaranteed for every specimen or arbitrarily small applied field. The S. Hughes quotation attribution is only as printed; no independent historical claim.
findings.basis: Independent two-state partition-function counterexample and order distinction.

findings.source_claim: Domains 0.1mm to few mm, random orientations give M=0, applied field realigns all, removed field leaves permanent magnet.
findings.assessment: The two before/after drawings are qualitative arrows and regions, not microscopy or scale data. The drawn initial finite collection need not sum exactly to zero. Approximate macroscopic cancellation describes a prepared multidomain state. Domain sizes are not universally restricted to that range. Growth of favorably oriented domains by wall motion and rotation matters; page20 notes partly restore this distinction. Remanence depends on pinning, anisotropy, material/shape/history; not all domains necessarily remain fully aligned. Domains and crystallographic grains are different objects.
findings.basis: Read complete slide and notes; model/diagram assessment; supplemental official domain discussion.

findings.source_claim: Fully aligned iron about2.1T; annealed iron1T with external0.0002T, factor5000.
findings.assessment: 1/0.0002=5000 is correct. About2.1T is a saturation-polarization scale μ0M_s, not a universal external field of any iron shape, nor a limit on total B=μ0(H+M). If B0=μ0H_applied and demagnetizing effects are negligible, H≈159A/m, M≈7.956e5A/m, effective secant χ_SI≈4999 at the 1T point. This is not a constant permeability or a measured 2004 result. Source lacks specimen geometry, precise anneal, curve or uncertainty, so the exact1T/0.2mT operating point remains unverified. Saturation refers to the net ferromagnetic moments; it does not mean that every paired/core electron in iron acquires the same spin orientation.
findings.basis: Independent arithmetic, SI dimensional interpretation and saturation-scale comparison.

findings.source_claim: Compass array models domains; taps move boundaries; cannot see domain flips but can hear them; coil/amplifier/speaker iron roaring, copper none.
findings.assessment: Compass array is an analogy of local alignment/metastability, not a microscopic exchange model. The described audio is pickup emf from abrupt magnetization/flux changes, amplified into sound; wall jumps are an important mechanism, not literal audible atoms. Domains/wall motion can be imaged with suitable instruments, so cannot see is a naked-eye classroom limitation. Copper lacks ferromagnetic Barkhausen jumps, not every possible induced electrical signal. No video/audio or actual lab result was observed.
findings.basis: Complete notes read; Faraday-law interpretation and primary Kerr observation.

findings.source_claim: DC electromagnet magnetizes iron plate; it remains after switch-off and supports up to5kg; falling breaks domains.
findings.assessment: Remanent attraction is plausible but the exact support load is apparatus-dependent and not measured here. A5kg added mass corresponds to49.0N weight (plus plate/hardware), not a magnetic-field value. Magnetic holding depends on gap/area and circuit; magnetic pressure B²/(2μ0) is only an ideal small-gap estimate. Opening a magnetic circuit or shock can change magnetization; domains break is not a precise universal microscopic mechanism, nor proof of complete demagnetization. Remanence can reside in the electromagnet core as well as the plate; the drawing does not separate their contributions.
findings.basis: Independent force/unit check; source diagram has no field, area, gap or polarity sufficient to calculate holding force.

findings.source_claim: DC magnetizes rod; AC demagnetizes by running slower and slower.
findings.assessment: Standard AC demagnetization requires an alternating field whose amplitude is reduced gradually toward zero (or gradual withdrawal through decreasing amplitude). Lowering frequency alone is insufficient and can leave remanence. A Variac changes voltage amplitude, not line frequency. Page22 shows schematic alternative DC/AC paths, but no winding sense/turn count or measured field; rod N/S orientation is undetermined. Cached official J7 text shows AC/DC/Variac but does not specify a complete diminishing-amplitude protocol, so it cannot independently certify that a particular apparatus operation implements the correction. The supplemental text says110VAC while its photo labels120VAC; those nominal labels are not an independently measured supply value.
findings.basis: Physical shrinking-loop deduction, published demagnetized-state method and inspected J7 photo/text.

findings.source_claim: B vertical, H horizontal loop; H0 to0 to-H0; H0 removal leaves nonzeroB depending history.
findings.assessment: Axis directions are correct; upper branch is traversed from positive H toward negative H, lower branch on return, for the ordinary dissipative loop. Source gives no directional arrows, scales, sample parameters or measured points. At H=0 branches give +Br or -Br, not +H or -H (text error). H0 to-H0 gives only half-cycle; the return sweep closes a loop. Finite remanence is for the chosen magnetized history; a demagnetized state can have B=0 at H=0. B does not strictly plateau at arbitrarily high H once M saturates: dB/dH→μ0 in SI (1 in Gaussian). No coercivity, remanence magnitude or loop loss can be numerically extracted.
findings.basis: Independent branch/history and constitutive-limit checks.

findings.source_claim: Oscilloscope x is primary I (H), y secondary I (B).
findings.assessment: Scope normally measures voltage. A series shunt gives x∝I_primary, approximately H under a specified magnetic-circuit model and sufficiently small secondary loading. Secondary emf is -N_s dΦ/dt in SI, not B; integration and calibration are necessary. Loaded secondary current depends on its circuit and does not generally measure B. The cached J11 schematic actually labels y across4µF capacitor with10kΩ resistor (RC integrator) and x across1Ω primary shunt. Its prose contradicts itself: description says capacitor, instructions say secondary resistor/emf. Prefer the inspected schematic for this supplemental model; it does not prove actual2004 wiring.
findings.basis: Independent Faraday/circuit derivation plus personally inspected supplemental schematic.

findings.source_claim: J11 supplemental schematic10kΩ,4µF; text60Hz.
findings.assessment: Ideal circuit gives V_C/E=1/(1+iωRC); RC=0.04s, ωRC≈15.08 at60Hz. Thus V_C≈(1/RC)∫E dt∝-Φ≈-AB, with sign dependent on lead/winding conventions. Exact sinusoidal amplitude is0.99781 of the ideal-integrator estimate and phase differs by3.794°. This is a calculation from the cited diagram/nominal frequency, not instrument calibration or observed measurement. Secondary loading, winding loss, leakage, core nonuniformity and frequency-dependent losses prevent exact B-H recovery from the slide alone.
findings.basis: Independent analytic and numerical circuit check.

findings.source_claim: AboveTc ferromagnetism ends suddenly; ironTc770°C; iron nut drops and regains magnetism on cooling.
findings.assessment: 770°C≈1043K is appropriate for ordinary bulk iron. Thermal fluctuations destroy spontaneous long-range ferromagnetic order; they do not remove electron moments or forbid field-induced paramagnetism. Sudden apparatus release is a force threshold and is not proof of a discontinuous magnetization jump. Simple mean-field magnetization can tend continuously to zero atTc; material-specific transition behavior requires evidence. Source gives no nut alloy, thermometer or force calibration, so release does not establish exact specimenTc. Cached J10 text/photo supports the intended demonstration description, not its execution or measured temperature.
findings.basis: Primary materialTc and direct model/force-threshold distinction.

findings.assessment: The intended equations, signs and c/4π factors are correct for Gaussian microscopic/total-source E,B equations, or vacuum with total charge/current. Macroscopic media require care with free/bound sources and D,H. Source render has stray hollow square glyphs adjacent to some operators/derivatives; text extraction and readable remaining strokes recover the intended standard equations. A fresh full-page3x render preserves those glyphs, so no image-cache truncation was found. Holiday picture is decorative, not an experimental EM diagram.
findings.basis: Independent Maxwell form/dimension comparison and personally inspected original and fresh full-page render.

independent_analytic_deductions.deduction: T_orbit=2πr/v; |I|=e/T; |μ|=Iπr²/c=evr/(2c), while |L|=m_e vr. Negative electron charge gives μ=-eL/(2m_e c).
For μ=γL, torque gives dμ/dt=γμ×B; with fixed B, both μ² and μ·B are constant. Alignment is not implied by torque alone.

Induced-moment energy U=-χ_SI V B0²/(2μ0) in weak isotropic vacuum approximation gives F=χ_SI V∇B0²/(2μ0). For anisotropic body U=-V B0·χ·B0/(2μ0); orientation maximizes effective susceptibility, not determined by its sign alone.
SI ellipsoid H_int=H_a-NM, M=χH_int implies B_int/B0=(1+χ)/(1+Nχ). N=1 demonstrates a boundary-case failure of unqualified field strengthening/weakening.
Curl of B=H+4πM gives J_total=J_free+c∇×M in magnetostatics. Time dependence adds ∂P/∂t to bound current and (1/c)∂D/∂t to curl H; surface K_M=cM×n is necessary at boundaries.
Printed H=χM would imply B/H=1+4π/χ, which diverges asχ→0. Correct M=χH gives finite vacuum limit1. χ_SI=4πχ_G; each table row converted independently.
Independent noninteracting two-state moments E_±=∓μB have Z=2cosh(μB/kBT); M=nμtanh(μB/kBT) is nonlinear yet paramagnetic. Weak field gives linear response, strong field saturation.
Source1T/0.0002T=5000. Under negligible demagnetizing field andB0=μ0H, H≈159.15A/m andχ_SI≈4999 at that point. μ0M_s≈2.1T corresponds toM_s≈1.671e6A/m.
5kg added load has weight49.03N usingg=9.80665m/s². NoB or force model can be inferred without area/gap/circuit and plate weight.

From positive saturation decreasingH traverses upper branch to+Br atH=0 and negativeH atB=0; reverse sweep lower branch. SI loop loss per unit volume∮H dB hasunitsJ/m³; Gaussian counterpart(1/4π)∮H dB haserg/cm³. No numerical loss calculable from unscaled drawings.

ε_s=-N_s A dB/dt inSI. SeriesRC withY acrossC obeysRC dV_C/dt+V_C=ε_s; forωRC≫1, V_C≈-(N_s A/RC)B plus integration constant and polarity convention. Nominal schematic values giveωRC≈15.08 at60Hz; no actual transfer calibration claimed.
770°C+273.15=1043.15K. Mean-field m=tanh((Tc/T)m) yields m²≈3(Tc/T-1)/(Tc/T)^3 nearTc, tending continuously tozero: a sudden release does not by itself establish a discontinuity.
